_comment: First-voyage hints (scripts/tutorial.gd). Each shows once, the first time you meet that part of the game. Keep them short: what it is, and the one decision that matters.

welcome.title: Your first voyage
welcome.text:
You're in port. Time stops while a port screen is open. The Market buys and sells (hover a price to see why it is what it is); the Shipyard repairs and refits; the Tavern hires hands and hears rumours; the Governor and the Contracts tab give you work.

This town is going hungry (see the Town tab). Towns remember what you do: sell it food from your stores, or bring a cargo from where food is cheap, and it will greet you as a friend, sell cheaper and sign on for less. Cheat it, smuggle or sack it, and it remembers that too.

A first plan: buy a cheap good this port makes, and sell it where it's wanted. The map-mode list on the top bar shows the last prices you know elsewhere.

sailing.title: Setting sail
sailing.text:
Click the sea or a port to set a course; the route goes round the land. The wind matters: you're fast across it and slow into it. Space pauses, 1 2 3 set the speed. Food, water and wages go every day, so keep an eye on the top bar (hover anything for the breakdown).

C opens the crew and ship screen.

encounter.text: A ship at sea. Merchants are prizes, warships and hunters are danger, and attacking any nation's ship without their enemy's commission is piracy. A battle is turn-based: each officer acts once a round; the menu shows the odds. Hit her weak points to Break her. You can always run or strike your colours.

cove.text: A hidden cove can be your base: a place to store plunder, careen, build, recruit and hold prisoners. It needs a garrison, food and money, and the busier it is the easier it is to find.

siege.text: A siege runs day by day: scout first (it shows the weak side), silence the fort or starve them, and storm when the odds are good. A relief squadron is coming. Lift the siege and you can come back to it later, damage and all.

contracts.title: Work
contracts.text: Contracts are the surest work: pay, a deadline, and a promise. Employers remember how your last job ended, and some lie about the pay. A letter of marque from the governor makes raiding a nation's enemies lawful.
